article_sentences: Transport associations argue that independent drivers, many of whom have bought their vehicles through bank loans, will struggle to compete with a company-backed fleet.
They have pointed to expenses such as monthly loan instalments, insurance, permits and vehicle maintenance, which drivers must bear regardless of how much they earn.
At least four taxi and transport associations have approached Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, seeking intervention over Green SM's proposed operations in Bengaluru.

In their representation, they have called for transparency on the permissions and licences granted to the company, along with an independent assessment of its potential impact on local transport operators.
"We welcome the transition towards environmentally sustainable transportation.
However, such a transition must be implemented in a fair, transparent and inclusive manner, without discriminating against local operators," the associations said.
Nataraj Sharma, president of the Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations, said local operators would find it difficult to match the proposed fares.
Speaking to TOI, Sharma said there were currently no state government regulations governing fares charged by electric taxis.
He added that Green SM could potentially offer rides for less than Rs 8 per km, while existing operators use petrol, diesel, CNG and LPG-powered vehicles.
"We will not be able to offer prices as low as them," he said.
The federation has also raised concerns about the company's access to corporate funding, bulk vehicle purchases, its own booking app and fleet-management systems.
It believes these advantages could put independent drivers under pressure to lower fares, even as they continue to pay their loan instalments and meet operating costs.

stories.headline: Akvan intensifies into severe cyclone near Andhra coast
stories.title: Akvan intensifies into severe cyclone near Andhra coast
stories.summary: Visakhapatnam, Nov 18 : Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, looming over the central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a severe cyclone, and is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Friday. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) bulletin on Wednesday morning, the cyclonic storm moved very slowly north-northwestwards with the speed of three kmph during past six hours, intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lay centered at 0530 hours at about 580 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 650 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 730 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). Continuing to move north-northwestward, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of November 20, as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph. Prakhar Jain, Managing Director, Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority and Chief Executive Officer of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), said that the cyclone movement is being continuously monitored. Appropriate instructions are being issued to the district administrations. He said 13 teams of NDRF, 11 teams of SDRF and local fire brigades were ready for emergency relief operations. Due to the impact of Tapan, there will be very heavy rains in some places in coastal districts on Thursday and Friday. Heavy to very heavy rains are likely at isolated places. APSDMA has appealed to people in the coastal region not to leave their homes unless it is an emergency. Farmers have been advised to take precautionary measures in agricultural work. Meanwhile, Home Minister V. Anita reviewed the situation as 'Akvan' intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. Officials reported that 'Akvan' is moving at a sluggish pace of 3 km/h. It is expected to make landfall by the afternoon of Friday. Home Minister Anita directed the state machinery to remain on high alert for the next 48 hours. She directed officials to take measures to prevent loss of life and property. The cyclone is likely to impact the North Andhra region. The public has been advised to remain vigilant. The Home Minister said residents in coastal areas should avoid stepping out unless absolutely necessary. Residents in low-lying areas must move to relief centres as soon as instructed by the authorities, she said. (IANS)

article_sentences: As severe cyclonic storm Akvan changed its track from Machilipatnam earlier to north coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in less than a day, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a new bulletin with fresh rainfall alerts.

According to the latest bulletin, issued at 3 p.m., extremely heavy rainfall is likely to occur in the districts of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR), Anakapalli and Kakinada in coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 19.
The alert for these districts remains in place for November 20 too.

An orange alert has been issued for the districts of Parvathipuram Manyam, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari and West Godavari, since isolated very heavy rainfall is likely on November 19 and 20.

The system over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal continued to move slowly in the north-northwest direction, and was located at 8.30 a.m. about 570 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 580 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 590 km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 660 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 710 km south of Gopalpur and 770 km south of Puri in Odisha.
Unlike during Arnab and Murasu, when meteorologists could forecast a clear track of the cyclones, experts said that this time, tracking the new system has become challenging.
Meteorologists use eight to nine forecasting models to arrive at a consensus on the probable course of the system.
“But, this time, no two models are showing the same results.
Akvan has become a new case study for us, since we never experienced so much uncertainty,” said P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre.
This is why the IMD has said the landfall could happen anywhere between Narsapur in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha.
The system has also weakened from what was predicted earlier.
It was first forecast to become a very severe cyclonic storm; it is now expected to remain a severe cyclonic storm.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan: Odisha orders suspension of beach tourism, tightens transport safety measures

article_sentences: Odisha suspends beach tourism, boating and water sports and tightens transport safety measures as Cyclone Akvan brings warnings of rough seas, strong winds, heavy rainfall and waterlogging along coastal areas.

Bhubaneswar: The Office of the Special Relief Commissioner (SRC), Odisha, on Wednesday wrote to the state Tourism and Commerce & Transport departments, directing the concerned authorities to take immediate measures to ensure the safety of tourists, visitors, tourism staff and the general public in view of cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ over the Bay of Bengal and the warning issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The SRC instructions came as the coastal areas of Odisha are likely to experience rough sea conditions, strong winds, heavy rainfall, and waterlogging until November 20 due to the cyclonic storm.

“Beach tourism at vulnerable beaches -- including sea bathing, boating, water sports, pleasure cruises, and other marine tourism activities -- shall remain completely suspended until the situation returns to normal,” the SRC office instructed in the letter to Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Tourism Department.
It also directed that public entry to unsafe beaches, jetties, coastal viewing points and other vulnerable tourist spots be restricted.
The tourism officials have been asked to arrange barricades and display warning signboards at vulnerable places.
The SRC directed all hotels, resorts, and tour operators in coastal areas to alert guests about the possible impact of the cyclone and cancel outdoor excursion programs.
They have also been asked to follow instructions regarding evacuation or shelters, and to keep emergency contact numbers and essential supplies stocked.

It asked the tourism authorities to issue clear safety advisories in multiple languages and coordinate with the District Emergency Operation Centres (DEOC) and the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC).

Similarly, the SRC directed the Principal Secretary of the Commerce & Transport department to take emergency measures to ensure the safe movement of passenger and goods vehicles, particularly at night, in view of reduced visibility in coastal areas due to cyclone ‘Akvan’.

“Night patrolling shall be intensified in low-lying, flood-prone, accident-prone, and poorly lit stretches of National and State Highways, and an adequate number of reflective signages (warning boards) shall be installed,” the SRC directed.
It directed regular updates on weather, vulnerable roads, alternative routes and traffic restrictions through digital display boards, bus owners' associations and other channels.

article_sentences: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan has altered its trajectory and is set to make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha's Puri on November 20, prompting the eastern coastal state to augment its preparedness and move people to safety.

In the morning, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the cyclone would cross land between Nellore and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh around noon on November 20, as a severe cyclonic storm with a maximum sustained wind speed of 100-110 kmph, gusting up to 120 kmph.
It altered the forecast in the afternoon, saying the landfall would be between Narsapur and Puri with a maximum sustained wind speed of 90 to 100 kmph.

As the weather system picked up pace, moving over the Bay of Bengal at a speed of 7 kmph from 3 kmph in the morning, Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said, "We need to prepare accordingly, keeping in view the changing direction of the impending cyclone."
"The chief secretary and the special relief commissioner are in touch with the district collectors concerned.
Rescue and relief teams are also being positioned keeping in view the evolving situation," he told reporters.
The Minister said several districts have already started moving people from vulnerable places, mostly landslide-prone areas, to safety.
Apart from Ganjam, the government has identified 141 places as vulnerable to landslides.
People in such places in Koraput and Malkangiri were also being evacuated.

Officials said the strategy was being devised to cope with the calamity, mostly heavy rain in the State, as the IMD had forecast less than 100 kmph wind speed in the State even during the landfall period.
Odisha had been spared from the direct impact of back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu that battered Andhra Pradesh between October and November.
The eastern coastal state still bore the brunt as the very severe Cyclone Arnab triggered widespread flooding and multiple landslides in south Odisha.

stories.headline: Don't keep us in the dark, don't humiliate us: Omar Abdullah to Centre on statehood
stories.title: Don't keep us in the dark, don't humiliate us: Omar Abdullah to Centre on statehood
stories.summary: Mendhar, Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday attacked the BJP-led Centre over the denial of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir and wondered whether the party was deliberately deferring it till gets its own chief minister in the Union Territory. Abdullah said the repeated promise of statehood at an "appropriate time" has become meaningless. "If it is your wish not to restore statehood until the BJP has its own chief minister in Jammu and Kashmir, then say it openly. Tell the people clearly so that they are not kept under any illusion, and we are not humiliated repeatedly," he said, addressing a public rally in Mendhar township of Poonch district. The chief minister said it is more than two years since his government assumed office, but the Centre has yet to honour its commitment to restore statehood, which it had promised would be done after delimitation and the assembly election. "Even after waiting for two years and one month, we have been compelled to ask: Where has our state gone? Why is the restoration of statehood being delayed?" he asked. On the Centre's "appropriate time" deadline, Abdullah said, "What is the yardstick you have to measure this? What kind of scale will you use to decide that the time has finally come to restore our statehood?" He also accused the central dispensation of using security incidents to justify the continued delay, even though the elected government has no control over the police or law and order. Referring to the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and several terror incidents in Kulgam, Reasi, and Kishtwar over the past two years, the chief minister said the elected government is being made to account for failures in areas outside its jurisdiction. "We have no control over the police or law and order, yet we are told that because of the Pahalgam attack, perhaps statehood cannot be restored now. An incident takes place in Kulgam, and the same justification is given. An attack takes place in Reasi or Kishtwar, and again the same argument is put forward," he said. "How can you hold us responsible for matters over which we have no control? We have fulfilled our responsibilities in the areas entrusted to us. stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 18: The State Investigation Agency (SIA) Kashmir has scored a major courtroom victory after the NIA Court Srinagar rejected the bail application of an accused in a narco-terror conspiracy case. The Court passed the order on November 17, 2026, after hearing detailed arguments from both sides. The accused, Basharat Ali Poswal, son of Muhammad Siddiq Poswal, resident of Tad, Karnah in Kupwara district, presently residing at Bemina, Srinagar, is facing prosecution in FIR No. 19/2022 of Police Station CI-SIA Kashmir. He has been booked under stringent provisions of law of NDPS Act - Sections 8-A, 27-B and 29, UAPA - Sections 13, 18, 39 and 40 and IPC -Sections 120-B, 121, 121-A and 201. The case alleges a serious nexus between narcotics trafficking, unlawful activities and conspiracy against the State, including activities aimed at waging war against the nation. When the bail plea was filed, the Court directed the prosecution to file objections. SIA Kashmir filed comprehensive, well-reasoned objections opposing bail. The matter was argued over several hearings. The prosecution highlighted the gravity of the allegations, the nature of the offences and the strict statutory bars on bail under the UAPA and NDPS Act. Charges against all accused persons were already framed by order dated July 15, 2026. The case is now listed for recording of prosecution evidence. With the rejection of bail, the trial will proceed without the accused being released from custody. In a statement, SIA Kashmir said the outcome reflects the dedication, legal skill and professional commitment of the agency. “SIA Kashmir remains firmly resolved to dismantle the narco-terror ecosystem and to prosecute effectively everyone involved in activities that threaten the peace, security and integrity of the nation,” the statement said. Police told the Supreme Court that social media content creators, reel-makers and other individuals carrying cameras and microphones could not be equated with bona fide journalists and were not entitled to the protections extended to accredited mediapersons.

The bench transferred the cases observing that it would not take up each case individually, because that would require a factual appreciation which would consume a lot of time.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V Mohana transferred the matters invoking Article 142 of the Constitution.
It revived the writ petitions and sent them to the High Court, requesting the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court to assign a Division Bench that would hear the matters on a daily basis.

The matter relates to civil appeals, contempt petitions, miscellaneous applications, review petitions and curative petitions, concerning land in Delhi acquired by the Union government, the Delhi government, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), the Airport Authority of India (AAI), and other agencies.
The bench noted that some acquisitions had been initiated as far back as in 1950.

All the acquisitions took place before 01.01.2014, when the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 came into force, and were made under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Observing that the right to be heard arises before any final action is taken under Section 20(3) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the high court had held that the Lokpal was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice.

Section 20(3) of the Act requires a Lokpal bench of at least three members to review preliminary inquiry reports under Section 20(2), hear the public servant, decide if a prima facie case exists and choose one or more actions.
The Lokpal probes allegations of corruption under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against specified public servants, politicians and certain institutions.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submissions of Sen's lawyer and issued the notice to the ombudsman.
The bench, however, refused to stay the proceedings before the Lokpal against Sen and said that the matter would be taken up after a week.
The proceedings originated from a preliminary inquiry conducted by the CBI on the directions of the Lokpal.
The CBI submitted its preliminary inquiry report on January 27, following which the Lokpal examined the allegations and found certain of them against Sen to be prima facie substantiated.
The Lokpal subsequently issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner, calling upon him to respond to the two allegations and providing an opportunity of hearing under Section 20(3) of the Act.
Challenging the order and notice, Sen told the high court that the Lokpal had passed the February 25 order without giving him an opportunity of hearing.
It was further said that the Lokpal had already formed an opinion on the allegations, rendering the subsequent show-cause notice and hearing an empty formality.

article_sentences: The Centre, yet again, in the Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), sought “two or three weeks” more for the publication of the final report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on the Air India Flight 171 crash.
The crash at the Ahmedabad Airport killed 12 crew members and 229 passengers on June 12, 2025.
On July 28, the court was told that the report would be published anytime between the “middle of September”, with a buffer till the “end of October”.
“It is at the fag end,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the Union government and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), said.
Advocates Prashant Bhushan and Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for petitioner-NGO, Safety Matters Foundation, said the authorities have been repeatedly seeking adjournments in the case.
Mr. Mehta, on the other hand, denied any attempt to deliberately delay the report.
In July, the apex court had put on hold petitioners’ plea for a Court of Inquiry or a “fair, transparent, and technically sound investigation” in order to the wait for the report.
One of the petitioners is 91-year-old Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the father of Commander Sumeet Sabharwal, one of the pilots on the ill-fated aircraft.
At the time, the court had clarified that the trajectory of the litigation would depend on whether the AAIB report on the crash would be “well-merited and accepted.”

The petitions, which include one by a pilots’ body, have argued that an investigation of such a magnitude ought to have gone to an independent agency in accordance with international protocols to which India was a signatory.
However, the apex court had opted to wait for the report, reasoning that the AAIB probe had “substantially progressed.”
On Wednesday (November 18), Mr. Bhushan submitted that the probe had now been on for a year-and-a-half now.

stories.title: CJI Surya Kant Meets UN Special Rapporteur On Rights Of Persons With Disabilities, Says Supreme Court Will Set Up Committee On Disability Rights

article_sentences: The Supreme Court will set up a Permanent Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant announced on Wednesday.

The CJI also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to constitute panels of young lawyers and sign language interpreters to assist advocates with disabilities in proceedings before the Court.

The announcements were made during a meeting between the CJI and Ms. Heba Hagrass, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, at the Supreme Court on November 18.
Lawyers with disabilities and representatives of civil society also participated in the meeting.
Emphasising that ensuring the rights of persons with disabilities is a constitutional obligation, the CJI said that equality is a fundamental principle of the Constitution.
He stressed the need to identify gaps in the implementation of laws and policies to ensure that persons with disabilities can exercise their rights in practice.
Referring to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged the steps taken by the Government and the judiciary over the past decade.
He also highlighted the role of courts in addressing administrative delays that prevent persons with disabilities from accessing benefits under laws and welfare schemes.
The CJI said that courts can issue writs of continuing mandamus directing public authorities to discharge their statutory obligations and monitor compliance until the required action is taken.
He further highlighted the contribution of public interest litigation in helping persons with disabilities enforce their rights.
Referring to Article 142 of the Constitution, he noted that the provision empowers the Supreme Court to do complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

The CJI also spoke about measures undertaken within the judiciary to promote the representation of persons with disabilities, including reservation in judicial and higher judicial services and relaxation of qualifying marks for eligible candidates with disabilities.

article_sentences: The petitioners also sought directions to allow ASDD voters to submit enumeration forms instead of filing Form 6 to restore their names.

An application has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking directions to the Election Commission of India (ECI) to put in place safeguards against the alleged misuse of Form 7 objections for targeted deletion of voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi.

The application alleges that Form 7 objections are being misused to facilitate targeted mass deletions of electors, particularly those belonging to specific communities, and seeks an impartial inquiry into alleged identity fraud and forgery.

The interlocutory application, filed by petitioners Anjali Bharadwal and Amrita Johri in their pending PIL challenging aspects of the Delhi SIR exercise, also seeks an impartial inquiry into alleged instances of forgery and identity fraud in the filing of Form 7 objections.

The petitioners have specifically referred to a reported instance in Delhi's Mustafabad Assembly Constituency, where 787 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of Muslim electors were allegedly filed in the names of 20 BJP Booth Level Agents (BLAs).
Citing a report published in The Hindu, the petitioners stated that at least 16 of the 20 BLAs denied having filed or authorised the applications.
One of the BLAs, Ankit Yadav, reportedly said that his details had been used to seek deletion of Muslim neighbours with whom he shared cordial relations.

The petitioners contend that these instances raise serious concerns about the authenticity of objections and the possibility of Form 7 being used as an instrument for systemic and targeted deletion of electors.

They have sought directions to the ECI to conduct a comprehensive audit of Form 7 applications filed across Delhi during the SIR exercise and verify whether the persons named as objectors had actually authorised and signed the applications.

They have also sought registration of FIRs wherever cognisable offences, including forgery, criminal impersonation and identity fraud, are disclosed, and strict action under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, against persons found to have knowingly submitted false declarations.

The petitioners have sought directions to the ECI to ensure that all Form 7 objections are publicly disclosed and that every Booth Level Agent filing an objection expressly identifies their status as a BLA.
They have further sought a direction that this status be reflected in the corresponding Form 10 disclosures.

article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces, with rewards of up to ₹1.5 lakh for individual weapons and sanctioning powers extending to ₹1 crore.
The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

According to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the reward amount will depend on the type and number of weapons recovered, including automatic and semi-automatic firearms, other weapons and ammunition.
The government said Maoists had, over the years, looted weapons belonging to State security forces during attacks on police stations and police personnel.

While existing provisions provide rewards for information leading to the arrest of Maoists and additional financial assistance to those surrendering with weapons, there was no specific provision for rewarding individuals who helped recover weapons previously looted from security forces.
The Home Department subsequently proposed a separate reward mechanism to facilitate the recovery of these weapons, which received Cabinet approval on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Under the scheme, Superintendents of Police will have the authority to sanction rewards of up to ₹10 lakh, while the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Gadchiroli Range, can approve amounts exceeding ₹10 lakh and up to ₹25 lakh.

Rewards exceeding ₹25 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh will require approval from the Special Inspector General of Police, Anti-Naxal Operations, while the Additional Director General of Police (Special Operations) will be authorised to approve rewards exceeding ₹50 lakh and up to ₹1 crore.
The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities.

In its statement, the government said coordinated efforts by the Centre and the State had weakened the influence of Maoist organisations in the region, particularly in Gadchiroli and Gondia, which it described as having become Naxal-free.
The government also said several development projects were being implemented in these districts as part of efforts to transform areas previously affected by Left-wing extremism.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to list a plea seeking the removal of social media videos featuring an Italian politician allegedly questioning the country's democratic system during the Bharat Summit 2026 organised by the Telangana Government in Hyderabad on November 13-14.

The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by Advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmad, who sought urgent intervention to take down the videos featuring Giacomo Filibeck, Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists.

Describing the remarks as a direct intervention in India's democratic affairs, the counsel said that the Italian delegate had not only raised the slogan but also translated it for other delegates attending the event.
"There was a summit organised by the main Opposition.
Foreign invitees were also there and one person from Italy, he represents the European Socialist Party, directly intervened in the bona fide Indian democratic system.
He used a very abusive slogan, since the urgency is of pulling down that slogan from social media, I need not repeat it here.

And it appears, the Italian delegate translates the slogan for other delegates, and on my soil he is saying the government is corrupt here and it is not bona fide and that he will work with the opposition to restore democracy.
It is a grave violation; it requires your intervention to pull down the video," Ahmed submited.
Responding to the mentioning, CJI Surya Kant asked whether the matter could be listed on the day after Friday.
The counsel agreed.
"Rest you argue before the concerned bench," the CJI said.

stories.headline: Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day ‘anti-terror conference’ in New Delhi tomorrow
stories.title: Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day ‘anti-terror conference’ in New Delhi tomorrow
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 18: In line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah will inaugurate the two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on Thursday, 19th November 2026. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference will deliberate on the theme 'Cross-Border Terrorism'. Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies / forces, an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism. In keeping with the 'Whole of Government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy. The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, and emerging hybrid threats to national security. Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges. This year, the conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for State police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the Government to improve prosecution. Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations. The conference will be attended by senior police officers of States and Union Territories, officers of Central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.

stories.headline: Trump faces key China issues ahead of meeting with Xi
stories.title: Trump faces key China issues ahead of meeting with Xi
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 18 : US President Donald Trump heads into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week amid divisions within his administration over restricting China's access to advanced technology, even as Washington and Beijing pursue cooperation on artificial intelligence risks and seek to preserve their trade truce. The White House schedule places their bilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, followed by three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. China's Foreign Ministry has separately confirmed the trilateral meeting for November 19. The New York Times reported Tuesday that the disagreement over technology restrictions extends beyond Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and much of the National Security Council staff have supported broader limits on China's access to advanced AI chips, while Lutnick pushed for a softer approach, the newspaper reported, citing current and former officials familiar with the discussions. The Times also reported concerns among advocates of a tougher China policy that Trump could reverse recently announced restrictions or use them as bargaining material in talks with Xi. Those concerns do not establish that Trump intends to offer such a concession. Former national security advisor H.R. McMaster told the newspaper that Trump's confidence in his negotiating ability could undermine a consistent approach to Beijing. "I think President Trump is often impeded by his belief that he can get the deal nobody else can get," McMaster said. The administration announced restrictions Monday aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced American computing technology remotely through overseas data centres. But technology competition is only one part of the relationship. The Washington Post highlighted parallel efforts to manage AI risks through model-testing cooperation and an incident-notification channel. Bessent said Washington and Beijing had begun a dialogue intended to reduce shared risks and prevent misunderstandings. He outlined plans to exchange practices for evaluating advanced AI models before their release and to establish a direct channel for the two countries to alert each other about any serious incidents involving their models. Bessent also described the administration's broader economic approach: "our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple." Critical-mineral supplies present another test of whether diplomatic agreements can produce dependable commercial outcomes -- an issue with direct relevance to India's manufacturing ambitions. A November 10 analysis by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies found that US imports of the covered rare-earth compounds and metals from China averaged 19.3 metric tonnes a month between November 2025 and September 2026. That compared with a monthly average of 76.8 metric tonnes before Beijing's April 2025 restrictions, a decline of about 75 per cent. India also depends heavily on Chinese supplies of permanent magnets. An Indian government background paper published in December 2025 said China accounted for between 84.8 per cent and 90.4 per cent of India's permanent-magnet imports by quantity during the financial years 2022-23 through 2024-25. India has approved a Rs 7,280 crore scheme intended to establish domestic manufacturing capacity of 6,000 metric tons annually for sintered rare-earth permanent magnets. The materials are important for electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics, aerospace and defence. Trump's engagement with India and other regional partners adds a strategic dimension to the China visit. At a November 9 CSIS briefing, Edgard Kagan, the organisation's senior adviser and Freeman chair in China studies, said a Quad meeting before Trump's China talks would remind Beijing of Washington's significant regional relationships. The Quad leaders met in Manila on Tuesday. They discussed Iran, safe navigation and energy security, and affirmed cooperation on critical-mineral supply chains. The Shenzhen talks will take place against that combination of strategic competition, commercial dependence and efforts to manage technological risks. (IANS)

article_sentences: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on May 10 confirmed that India had agreed to a ceasefire with Pakistan after the latter reached out.

Shortly before that, US President Donald Trump stated that India and Pakistan had agreed to a “full and immediate ceasefire” after a fourth day of strikes and counter-strikes against each other’s military installations.
“The Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) of Pakistan called the DGMO of India at 1530 hours (3.30 pm) this afternoon.
It was agreed between them that both sides would cease all firing and military action on land, in the air, and at sea with effect from 1700 hours (5 pm),” Misri told media.
The Foreign Secretary, in a brief press conference announcing the ceasefire agreement, added, “Instructions have been given on both sides to implement this understanding.
The Directors General of Military Operations will speak again on May 12.
Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also said both countries had agreed to a ceasefire “with immediate effect”.

On the social media platform Truth Social, Trump wrote: “After a long night of talks mediated by the United States, I am pleased to announce that India and Pakistan have agreed to a FULL AND IMMEDIATE CEASEFIRE.
Congratulations to both Countries on using Common Sense and Great Intelligence.”

The ceasefire announcement followed fears that both countries’ nuclear arsenals might come into play, as the Pakistan military said a top military and civil body overseeing its nuclear weapons would meet.
But Dar later said no such meeting was scheduled.
At the same time, officials from both sides showed a willingness, for now, to take a step back following the day’s exchanges, while the civilian death toll on both sides of the border mounted to 66.

stories.summary: Mendhar, Nov 18: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday laid the foundation stones and inaugurated 13 development projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in the border town of Mendhar in Poonch district, aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public service delivery. The projects cover key sectors, including power, flood protection, road connectivity, education and water supply, an official spokesman said. He said the projects include the laying of foundation stones for a 50 MVA Grid Sub-Station at Mendhar and flood protection works along Mendhari Nallah, besides key infrastructure projects in road connectivity, education and water supply. During the programme, the chief minister also flagged off Jammu and Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation (SRTC) bus services on three new routes and two new water tankers to improve public transport and drinking water supply in Mendhar. The spokesman said the chief minister's visit underscored the government's commitment to strengthening essential infrastructure, improving public services and accelerating development in remote and border areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
